assessments.reasoning: Classification of List Forms describes dispatch based on the first position of a nonempty list and leaves that element unevaluated as a form. The following section distinguishes function-cell indirection from ordinary evaluation.

challenge.method: Check a symbol with an indirect function definition, an anonymous lambda in first position, and an unrecognized function-position object. Compare an empty list and the Scheme contrast in the GNU text.
challenge.results: Inspecting first position and resolving a symbol's function cell are part of dispatch. A first-position lambda is accepted directly. Invalid or autoload cases use their own rules. The three named paths apply to the recognized kinds.

limitations: The claim covers classification of valid nonempty list forms in GNU Emacs 29.4 and keeps call-argument treatment and other Lisp evaluators distinct.
